title: Neural Network Field Theory at Finite Width
abstract: Under mild assumptions, any quantum mechanical (QM) model or quantum field theory (QFT) admits a representation in terms of an ensemble of neural networks with countably many random parameters. We investigate the features of NN-QM and NN-FT models with finitely many parameters, such as a feedforward network of width $N < \infty$. We find that, generically, such models must violate one of the properties of conventional Euclidean QFTs, such as reflection positivity or cluster decomposition. We present several complementary ways of understanding which features can and cannot be preserved at finite $N$, both in QM and in QFT.
summary: This work explores the theoretical limits of representing quantum field theories using neural networks with a finite number of parameters. The authors demonstrate that such finite truncations generically fail to satisfy core physical axioms, such as reflection positivity, because the underlying mathematical structure required by QFTs is too complex for finite sums to capture. This sets a fundamental boundary on what ML models can simulate in quantum physics.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether Quantum Mechanical (QM) and Quantum Field Theory (QFT) models can be accurately represented using Neural Networks (NNs) with a finite number of parameters.
main_result: Generically, finite-width NN models are incapable of reproducing the correlation functions of conventional, non-trivial QFTs or QM systems because they violate fundamental properties like reflection positivity or cluster decomposition.
method: The authors compare the correlation functions derived from finite-width NN architectures (e.g., using finite sums of basis functions) against the known requirements of QFTs, such as the Källén-Lehmann representation.
model_or_system: The study concerns the representation of quantum systems, ranging from 1D QM models (path integrals) to general QFTs, using NN ensembles parameterized by a finite set of weights.
key_observables: Correlation functions $\langle \phi(x_1) \cdots \phi(x_n) angle$, the connected two-point function (covariance kernel), and the adherence to the Källén-Lehmann representation.
important_parameters: The crucial parameter is the finite width $N$ of the neural network architecture, contrasting with the infinite parameters required for exact representation.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a true QFT obeying standard axioms (like OS axioms) and focuses on the limitations imposed by truncating the representation to finite $N$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general framework for NN representations of QFTs, then analyzes the 1D QM case using the two-point function, and finally extends the obstruction argument to general QFTs by considering distributional neurons.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical constraint on the complexity of physical theories that can be encoded or simulated by finite-parameter machine learning models, linking fundamental physics axioms to computational limitations.
